Spatial kriging of SHmax axes after van den Boogaart & Schaeben (2002)

Source: R/interpolation_krige.R
krige.Rd

Ordinary kriging of the axial orientation tensors, with a distance-only trace variogram (isotropy of measurements). The kriged tensor is decomposed with the eigenvalue method of ot_eigen2d(). The per-observation uncertainty, given as a standard deviation in degrees, is used as measurement error on the diagonal of the kriging matrix.

Usage

circular_krige(
  x,
  grid = NULL,
  lon_range = NULL,
  lat_range = NULL,
  gridsize = 2,
  R_range = 300,
  max_data = 50,
  min_data = 3L,
  min_dist_threshold = 200,
  vgm_model = c("spherical", "exponential", "gaussian"),
  nugget = 0,
  range_km = 300,
  sill = NULL,
  use_uncertainty = TRUE
)

PoR_circular_krige(
  x,
  PoR,
  grid = NULL,
  PoR_grid = TRUE,
  lon_range = NULL,
  lat_range = NULL,
  gridsize = 2.5,
  remove_PoR = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

sf object containing

azi

angles in degrees (e.g. orientation of \(\sigma_\text{Hmax}\))

unc

(optional) Uncertainties of azi in degree

type

(optional) Methods used for the determination of the direction of \(\sigma_\text{Hmax}\)

grid

(optional) Point object of class sf.

lon_range, lat_range

(optional) numeric vector specifying the minimum and maximum longitudes and latitudes (ignored if grid is specified).

gridsize

numeric. Target spacing of the regular grid in decimal degree. Default is 2.5. (is ignored if grid is specified)

R_range

numeric value or vector of search radii in km. Only observations within the radius are used.

max_data

integer. The number of nearest observations used for each prediction. Default is 50.

min_data

integer. If the number of observations within distance R_range is less than min_data, a missing value NA will be generated. Default is 3 for circular_idw() and 4 for circular_idw_stats().

min_dist_threshold

numeric. Distance threshold for smallest distance of the prediction location to the next observation location. Default is 200 km.

vgm_model

Variogram model: "spherical" (default), "exponential" or "gaussian".

nugget

numeric in \([0, 1)\). Nugget of the trace variogram.

range_km

numeric. Range of the variogram model in km.

sill

numeric in \((\text{nugget}, 1]\). Sill of the trace variogram. If NULL (default), it is set to \(1 - \bar{R}^2\), where \(\bar{R}\) is the mean resultant length of the doubled angles of x$azi.

use_uncertainty

logical. If TRUE (default), unc (standard deviation in degrees) is used as measurement error.

PoR

Pole of Rotation. data.frame or object of class "euler.pole" containing the geographical coordinates of the Euler pole

PoR_grid

logical. Whether the grid should be generated based on the coordinate range in the PoR (TRUE, the default) CRS or the geographical CRS (FALSE). Is ignored if grid is specified.

remove_PoR

logical. Whether PoR azimuths and coordinates will be removed from final output or not (the default.)

...

Arguments passed to circular_krige()

Value

sf object containing

lon,lat

longitude and latitude in degrees

azi

kriged axis direction in degrees (0 to 180), the principal direction from ot_eigen2d()

sd

circular standard deviation of the axis in degrees, computed from conf as rad2deg(sqrt(-2 log(conf))) / 2

R

search radius in km

mdr

mean distance between grid point and data / R

N

number of observations used

conf

confidence in \([0, 1]\), \(2 \lambda_1 - 1\), i.e. the axial strength relative to the trace of the kriged tensor

kvar

kriging variance on the trace-variogram scale

eig1

largest eigenvalue of the kriged tensor (axial strength), in \([0.5, 1]\). The smaller eigenvalue, \(1 = \lambda_1\), is the axial dispersion

Attribute "vgm" records the variogram parameters used.

Details

The method is the simplified ordinary-kriging form derived by van den Boogaart & Schaeben (2002) for axes in the embedding \(u u^T\). Their isotropy-of-measurements assumption gives the trace variogram used here. The kriged tensor is \(\sum_i \lambda_i u_i u_i^T\), computed by ot_eigen2d() with the kriging weights as weights. The principal direction is the eigenvector of the largest eigenvalue, and the eigenvalues sum to one. Their values give the strength and dispersion of the prediction.

Fit nugget, sill, and range_km to the empirical variogram from variogram_axial().

Note

Only axial (180° periodic) data are supported.

References

van den Boogaart, K.G. and Schaeben, H. (2002). Kriging of regionalized directions, axes, and orientations I. Mathematical Geology, 34(5), 479-503.

See also

variogram_axial() for computing the empirical variogram of axial data; ortensor2d() and ot_eigen2d() for the orientation tensor and its eigenvalue decomposition.

Other smoothing: PoR_idw, idw, smooth

Examples

data("san_andreas")
v <- variogram_axial(san_andreas)
res <- circular_krige(san_andreas, R_range = 300,
                           vgm_model = "spherical",
                           nugget = 0.25, range_km = 1000)
